doc.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Parents and siblings: father's death, mother's work, brothers
summary: His parents came from Virginia; his father, a mechanic, died when he was six, and his mother cleaned offices. He names his brothers and sisters.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay. If we could for the record, if you could give us your parents name and where they came from originally.
Well my mother’s name was Elizabeth Day.
[spells] D-A-Y?

[spells] D-A-Y, that was her maiden name, last name Burrell, of course. And my father’s name was William Henry Burrell. They were both from Virginia. My mother was from an area near Amsterdam called Roanoke. I’m not sure of the area that my father was from, but he was also from Virginia.
And your father’s occupation?
He was a mechanic, yeah.
What type of mechanic, do you…
Automobile…
Automobile, okay.
But I think it was not necessarily a, as we think of now, top pro. I think it was just a something that he learned and picked up and was doing that for a living.
Did he work at one of the major plants?
No, but I did later on. I worked at Ford for a few years, yeah.
And your mother?
My mother was…
Homemaker, no?
Homemaker, but also my father died when I was six years old.
What did he die from?

I’m not sure. So my mother went to work and I remember a couple of jobs that she had, which I, she would take me with her sometimes because there were no babysitters. It was cleaning offices in office buildings, you know, she would be the maintenance person to clean offices and that was it.
So I know having done some research about your background, I know that you’re one of, you’re the youngest of three brothers, surviving three children of six.

Yes, I am the youngest. My other brother, the middle brother, was Donald Burrell. And the oldest brother was William Henry, Jr. and there were three sisters before that. Let’s see, I think their names were Hazel, Blossom, and I can’t think of the other one at the moment.
But all older than you?
Yeah.
And the cause of death for all…
They…childhood diseases at that time that they didn’t have cures for, diphtheria…
So they died in infancy?
Yeah, yeah. Well, not infancy, but earlier on.
